tier_reason: The README gives only absolute figures for this port (1.4 GiB/s and 7.7 s per 1e9 64-bit values on a Core i7-8650U) and no measurement of any baseline (std::ranlux48, RANLUX, mt19937); ranluxpp-test.c only times its own loop with clock_gettime. With no comparison in the repo the entry stays at D.

corrections.caveats: No measurement against any baseline in the repo, so tier D; 0 stars, 0 forks, 15 commits. The README (opened) says the code combines Sibidanov's ranluxpp with ROOT's portable implementation converted from C++ to C, so it is a port of two already-listed entries (sibidanov/ranluxpp, paper:root-ranluxpp). Repo figures: 1.4 GiB/s and 7.7 s per 1e9 64-bit values on a Core i7-8650U, about 7.7 ns per value (derived from page data). Third-party figures for the other implementations (ROOT blog: portable RANLUX++ about 9 ns, Sibidanov's assembly about 8 ns, TRandom1 RANLUX about 62 ns, TRandom3 Mersenne Twister about 3 ns) mean RANLUX++ beats RANLUX but not Mersenne Twister. The Hahnfeld-Moneta paper (arXiv 2106.02504) was blocked. Library files are under ROOT's LGPL-2.1-or-later terms (LICENSE), while ranluxpp-test.c carries a GPL-3.0-or-later header. Last commit 2021-06-22.

notes: The README says this is a C conversion of ROOT's portable RANLUX++ merged with Sibidanov's code. Both are already listed, and the repo adds no numbers against a baseline, so fold it into paper:root-ranluxpp as a duplicate (port). The evidence is not invalid; if kept, keep it at tier D with these caveats. Metadata checked on github.com (0 stars, 15 commits, not a fork, not archived, last commit 2021-06-22).

tier_reason: benchmark_url is null. The README and the bundled doc/ug.pdf user guide (version 3.0.1, 2013-08-27; read with pdftotext) cite KLU, SuperLU and PARDISO only as related work and contain no timings or speedups, so the repo has no evidence of its own and stays at D.

corrections.caveats: Third-party mirror (6 commits by wibraun, 2018-05-24 to 2018-09-04) of the open-source NICSLU 3.0.1 (Copyright 2011-2013 Tsinghua University, Xiaoming Chen); no benchmark numbers in the repo or doc/ug.pdf. License is LGPL-2.1-or-later, but source/nicslu_mc64.c (its header says it is modified from mc64ad.c in SuperLU_DIST) carries the HSL MC64 restrictions raised in open issue #1 'MC64 conditions on external use' (opened 2018-12-11 by rwl, no reply): acknowledge in publications, share modifications with the authors, and 'shall not pass this code directly to a third party without the express prior consent of the authors'. These go beyond the LGPL, hence usability mixed. README: gcc -O2 only, 'CANNOT be -O3'. The closed NICSLU entry's enrichment reports that the author's FAQ calls this version old and buggy, with the closed version up to 3x faster. The paper speedups over KLU (2.08x-8.57x, 1-12 threads) were seen only as search snippets and may describe a later NICSLU. Newer solvers (CKTSO, GLU3.0) are reported to beat NICSLU. Last commit 2018-09-04.

notes: Catalog rule: wibraun/NICSLU carries no evidence of its own (no numbers in the README or ug.pdf), so fold it into https://github.com/chenxm1986/nicslu as a duplicate, adding there that this LGPL-2.1-or-later 3.0.1 mirror is the only source release, with an HSL MC64 licensing restriction (issue #1).
